title: Email Validator
description: Validate email syntax in the browser with clear warnings and no DNS, domain, or mailbox checks.
metaDescription: Validate email syntax in the browser with clear warnings and no DNS, domain, or mailbox checks.

form.title: Validate email
form.description: Type or paste an address to check whether its format is accepted by common forms.

input.title: Email
input.label: Email address
input.privacy: Validation runs in your browser. This tool does not send the email to the server.
input.hint: Single-address validation only. Lists, display names, and mailboxes are not verified.

share.title: Share
share.description: By default, the link stores only the tool route.
share.safe: The current link does not include the typed email.
share.publicWarning: Links with an email expose the address to anyone who receives the URL.
share.tooLong: The email is too large for a safe link. The link will include only the content option.

result.title: Result
result.description: The result shows syntax and warnings, not existence or delivery.
result.emptyDescription: Enter an address to start validation.
result.validDescription: The format is accepted by common email forms.
result.attentionDescription: The address may depend on internationalized email support or was normalized before validation.
result.normalizedHint: The domain was lowercased or converted to ASCII when needed. The local part was preserved.
result.syntaxOnly: Syntax validation only. Does not check DNS, MX, SMTP, existing domains, or mailboxes.

input.label: Input
input.pass: Length and basic characters are within the expected range.

atSign.label: At sign
atSign.pass: There is exactly one @ separating user and domain.

localPart.label: Local part
localPart.pass: The part before @ uses common characters and valid dots.

domain.label: Domain
domain.pass: The domain has syntactically valid labels.

unsupportedSyntax.label: Uncommon syntax
unsupportedSyntax.pass: No unusual RFC form was detected.

normalization.label: Normalization
normalization.pass: No adjustment was needed beyond reading the text.

issues.empty: There is no email to validate yet.
issues.trimmedWhitespace: Leading or trailing spaces were ignored for validation.
issues.inputTooLong: The input exceeds this tool's practical length limit.
issues.asciiControl: Remove line breaks, tabs, or control characters.
issues.internalWhitespace: Common email addresses do not allow spaces inside the address.
issues.missingAt: Include an @ sign between the local part and the domain.
issues.multipleAt: Use only one @ sign in the address.
issues.localPartTooLong: The part before @ is too long for a common email address.
issues.localPartStartsWithDot: The local part should not start with a dot.
issues.localPartEndsWithDot: The local part should not end with a dot.
issues.localPartConsecutiveDots: The local part should not contain consecutive dots.
issues.localPartInvalidCharacters: The local part contains characters outside the common format.
issues.nonAsciiLocalPart: Unicode characters before @ may be valid with SMTPUTF8, but not all forms and servers accept them.
issues.displayNameUnsupported: Display names next to the address are not accepted in this version.
issues.quotedLocalPartUnsupported: Quoted addresses are allowed by some RFC rules but rejected by many common forms.
issues.commentsUnsupported: Comments in parentheses are not accepted in this version.
issues.domainLiteralUnsupported: Domain literals like [192.0.2.1] are not accepted in this version.
issues.multipleAddressesUnsupported: Validate one email at a time.
issues.domainIdnNormalized: The internationalized domain was converted to ASCII/punycode for validation.
issues.domainInvalidIdn: The internationalized domain could not be interpreted safely.
issues.domainNeedsDot: Use a domain with at least one dot, such as example.com.
issues.domainEmptyLabel: The domain has a duplicate, leading, or trailing dot.
issues.domainTooLong: The domain exceeds the practical 253-character limit.
issues.domainLabelStartsOrEndsWithHyphen: Each domain part must start and end with a letter or number.
issues.domainInvalidCharacters: The domain contains characters outside letters, numbers, hyphens, and dots.
issues.syntaxOnly: Valid syntax does not prove that the domain exists, has MX records, accepts SMTP, or that the mailbox exists.

summary.syntaxOnly: Scope: syntax validation only, without DNS/MX/SMTP/mailbox checks.

details.title: What this validation covers
details.description: The first version prioritizes behavior expected by common forms, not every possible RFC case.

syntax.title: Common syntax
syntax.description: Checks one @, local part, domain labels, and dot placement.

dns.title: No DNS or MX
dns.description: Does not make external lookups or confirm that the domain receives email.

rfc.title: Broader RFCs
rfc.description: Quoted strings, comments, display names, and domain literals are outside v1.

unicode.title: Internationalized email
unicode.description: Domains can be normalized to punycode; Unicode before @ triggers a warning.

privacy.title: Link privacy
privacy.description: The email enters the link only if the explicit share-content option is checked.

privacy.question: Is the email sent to the server?
privacy.answer: No. Validation runs in the browser. The email enters a URL only if you enable the option to include it in the link.

mailbox.question: Does this validator confirm that the mailbox exists?
mailbox.answer: No. It checks format. It does not confirm a person, inbox, delivery, bounce risk, or contact permission.

dnsMx.question: Does the validator check DNS or MX?
dnsMx.answer: No. There is no DNS, MX, SMTP, external API, or verification-email request.

unicode.question: Why does an email with accents or Unicode show a warning?
unicode.answer: SMTPUTF8 allows internationalized addresses in some environments, but support in forms and servers still varies.

rfc.question: Why are addresses with quotes, comments, or display names rejected?
rfc.answer: Those formats exist in broader email rules, but many common forms reject them. This tool prioritizes everyday syntax.

sharing.question: Can I share a link with a filled email?
sharing.answer: Yes, only after checking the option to include the email in the link. Do that only when anyone with the link may see the address.

seo.about: The email validator checks common syntax for a single address directly in the browser. It explains issues such as missing @, duplicate dots, malformed domains, unsupported characters, and internationalized cases.
seo.howToUse: Type or paste an email, read the status, and copy the normalized version when available. The tool does not check DNS, MX, SMTP, or mailbox existence; include the email in a shared link only when it may be visible to whoever receives the URL.
